terms.gloss: camp out, sleep in a tent
terms.comment: Our phrase. Sub pellibus, “under hides”, is Caesar’s and Livy’s for soldiers living in tents, which were made of leather; pernoctāre is to spend the night. No word for camping as a pastime is known; Traupman gives only the campsite and the tent.

terms.gloss: sleep out under the open sky
terms.comment: Sub dīvō, under the open sky, in the open air (Cic., Hor.).

phrases.english: he decided to winter in tents (Caesar, of his army)

sources: Lewis & Short: pellis · Lewis & Short: pernocto · Lewis & Short: divum
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 286, 392 (campsite and tent; no word for camping). Morgan–Owens has only the camping stove.
